answer.answer: The study's goal is met as counted: five settings on five different scenes failed in every repeat (S15, S1, S16, S17, S3). All five slow the lead car to 0.5x, four of them also shift it +1 s, and none needs planner delay. But only one of these is a real policy failure, and it is not a rear-end. The triage of the video and logs shows that every failure at S1, S3, S15 and S16 (and the single run at S4) happened while the ego was still replaying the recorded human drive. The slowed lead car's box was already overlapping the ego before the policy took control, and the failure was counted at the handoff moment. Those four are artifacts of retiming the lead car against a fixed logged ego path, not cases where VaVAM rear-ends a braking car. S17 (scene 19f339ba) is the only setting where the policy was at fault, in every run, and there it braked for no clear reason and steered left into a car in the next lane, with no lead car involved. So the study found no confirmed case of the policy rear-ending a slowing or stopping lead car.

findings.claim: On scenes 0e899dd3, 023b7fcc, 12855a41 and 096988dd, every run with the lead car at 0.5x speed failed, but each failure was a box overlap that began during the logged-ego replay, before the policy took control. The policy was not at fault in any of them, so these settings are replay artifacts, not challenging cases for the policy.

On scene 19f339ba (0.5x speed, +1 s), every run failed through the policy's own fault. After handoff, on a highway with no car ahead in its lane, it braked from about 17 to 11 m/s and steered left into a car in the adjacent lane. This is a real failure but a lane-keeping one, not a rear-end of the lead car.
On 023b7fcc, how the lead car was timed decided whether the replay produced contact: at 0.5x speed the run with no shift failed, but the single run shifted +1 s passed.

Scene 0dbb91dd did not fail with a +1 s shift and 0.5x speed, and adding 100 ms or 200 ms of planner delay did not make it fail. The single run at each delay was less critical than the run with no delay.

The closest calls for the policy itself were on 0cf6368d with the lead car at 0.5x speed, where criticality rose as the shift went from 0 s to +2 s without failing. Each setting has only a single run, and this scene's lead car is also a cut-in car.
Scene 09a95ffa passed its single run at both 0 s and +1 s with the lead car at 0.5x speed, and showed no criticality.

open: Whether VaVAM rear-ends a braking lead car at all is unsettled. Every lead-car contact counted here happened before handoff. Re-run 0e899dd3, 023b7fcc, 12855a41 and 096988dd with milder retiming (for example 0.7x to 0.9x speed, or shifts that keep the gap open until after the 4.7 s handoff), so that any closing happens while the policy is in control.
The validity gate did not flag these pre-handoff collisions: possible_artifacts is 0 on every row. Failures that are already present at handoff should be filtered out before the goal counts them.
Is the S17 lane drift on 19f339ba caused by the retiming, or does the policy do it with the recorded timing too? Run the scene unretimed and at 0.5x speed with a 0 s shift.
0cf6368d at +2 s and 0.5x speed (S9) was the closest policy-driven call. Repeat it, and try +2 s with 100 to 200 ms of delay, to see whether it tips into failure after handoff.
The study ran only lead-car speeds of 0.5x and shifts of 0 to +2 s. Negative shifts and speeds between 0.5x and 2x were not tested.
